subject: Recap: first-token latency targets, streaming concurrency & trial next steps
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Elena Gomez <elena@cloudscale.ai>, platform@cloudscale.ai
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-07T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: first-token latency needs + concurrency constraints (recap)

Hi Elena / CloudScale platform team,

Thanks again for taking the time this morning — I wanted to capture the key constraints and next steps so we have a single source of truth. Please correct anything I missed.

Quick summary of what you shared:
- Product: real-time summarization assistant for enterprise support queues (web & mobile streaming UX).
- Current stack: on-prem ingestion -> Kinesis -> upstream service calling an LLM endpoint (self-hosted model variants today).
- Pain: occasional visible freezes in the streaming UI; users complain at ~250–400ms spikes on initial token delivery and longer tails during bursts.
- Traffic shape: steady baseline ~120 concurrent streaming sessions per region, peak bursts to ~480 for 10–15 minute windows during morning escalations.
- Success criteria you gave: first-token p95 <= 300ms, steady-state per-token generation latency that keeps end-to-end UX smooth (no perceived stalls), and graceful degradation to a lower-cost model if capacity strained.

Measurements you can share (requested):
- 1) a 1-hour trace capture or representative log (we asked about 100–200 sample session traces)
- 2) sample prompt/response sequences (you agreed to share a 10k-line sample JSONL anonymized) — I attached a template for the schema.

Immediate ideas we discussed:
- prefix/KV caching for repeated context to reduce repeated encoding costs, which should reduce first-token time for follow-up requests;
- streaming-friendly model variants (smaller context-optimized quantized versions) for spikes;
- bounded batching with latency SLOs to preserve first-token latency while improving GPU utilization.

Next steps (owners / timing):
- CloudScale: drop the anonymized sample (stream_samples_10k.jsonl) into the shared GDrive link by EOD Fri (Elena).
- Hannah: provision a short Dedicated trial (2 GPU machines) for a 2-week acceptance window so you can run your traffic replay. I’ll start the paperwork and get Marcus and Monica looped on ops specifics.
- Aditya: prepare a draft of the trial commercial (trial credits, evaluation acceptance criteria) and share by Thu.
- Marcus / Monica (ops): prepare a checklist for observability access we need (trace samples, metric names, and a read-only S3/GCS role or temporary log bundle).

Attachments: p95_targets_v1.xlsx (template for acceptance matrix), stream_samples_schema.md (inline in the drive).

Thanks — I'll follow up with the trial order and the Drive link in a separate email.

Best,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
+1 415 555 0142

From: Elena Gomez <elena@cloudscale.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: platform@cloudscale.ai, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-07T18:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: first-token latency needs + concurrency constraints (recap)

Thanks Hannah — that matches our notes. A couple clarifications: 

1) The 250–400ms spikes are mostly first-token latency for brand-new sessions (not follow-ups).
2) During bursts the p99 can reach ~900ms — the UX team flags anything above 600ms as visibly janky.
3) We can export traces but they’ll be anonymized and delivered as a log bundle (S3 presigned link). Expect the 10k sample by Friday morning PST.

One ask: can your trial include a canary policy that routes 10% of traffic to a quantized variant and measures the perceived step-down in latency/quality? We want to see automated fallback in action.

Elena
Elena Gomez
Director, Platform Engineering — CloudScale.ai
elena@cloudscale.ai | +1 206 555 0180
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Elena Gomez <elena@cloudscale.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-08T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: first-token latency needs + concurrency constraints (recap)

Elena — happy to take the commercial piece. Two quick notes on the trial:

- Proposal: 2-week Dedicated trial (3 x A10G-equivalent GPUs) + trial credits to cover non-RW storage and networking.
- Acceptance matrix (high level): first-token p95 <= 300ms for 90% of test sessions from your replay, tail p99 <= 600ms for at least 80% of runs, and no more than 5% of sessions experiencing streaming stalls >1.5s. (Detailed spreadsheet attached.)
- Canary plan: we’ll set up policy to route 10% of traffic to a lower-precision quantized model and capture automatic rollback criteria based on a small human-eval prompt set + latency regression alerts. That meets your ask.

Planned timeline:
- Thu 4/9: legal + trial order (we’ll provision infra after signature).
- Fri 4/10: you upload sample dataset; Marcus/Monica request access to logs.
- Week of 4/13: trial live + initial replay runs.

If that sounds right I’ll assemble a short SOW and trial order.

Thanks,
Aditya
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Elena Gomez <elena@cloudscale.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-09T10:11:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: first-token latency needs + concurrency constraints (recap)

Elena — great, thanks for the clarifications and for committing the sample. A couple final operational notes before we kick off:

- Observability: Marcus will send a small script to validate metric names (redwood.accepted_latency_ms, redwood.kv_cache_hit_rate, redwood.stream_stall_count) and a short guide on required spans. If you can map them to your trace IDs that will speed analysis.
- Security: Monica will open the Private trial checklist — we support temporary S3 presigned uploads for trace bundles; if you prefer VPC peering we can handle that but it takes a few extra days.
- Evaluation: please confirm which three user journeys you want in the acceptance matrix (our default: new conversation start, mid-session follow-up, long-context summarization).

I’ll kick off the trial order once legal signs. Aditya — if you can share the draft SOW by end of day Thursday I’ll route it to procurement at CloudScale.

Thanks all — looking forward to getting the replay running.

Best,
Hannah
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
